NASA Invites Public to 'Adopt a Pixel' from Upcoming Roman Space Telescope Imagery

Participation in Cosmic Discovery

NASA has launched an outreach initiative allowing the public to claim a symbolic 'pixel' from the inaugural imagery produced by the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. By registering an email address on the official mission portal, participants are assigned a specific, unique coordinate from the telescope's future observational data. Upon registration, users receive a commemorative certificate representing their assigned portion of the cosmos, which the agency encourages sharing via social media.

Mission Objectives and Capabilities

Designed as a next-generation observatory, the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is engineered to explore critical mysteries in dark energy, exoplanetary research, and infrared astrophysics. Equipped with a 2.4-meter primary mirror and a Wide Field Instrument, the telescope provides a field of view 100 times larger than that of the Hubble Space Telescope's infrared instrument. This expansive view allows the observatory to survey significant portions of the sky with unprecedented efficiency.

User Impact and Guidelines

Registration is limited to one pixel per email address. NASA notes that if multiple family members wish to participate but share a single email account, they will be collectively assigned to a single pixel. Users are responsible for retaining their registration information, as the provided email address is the primary method for retrieving assigned pixel data once the mission commences operations. For official information and to participate in the project, visit the NASA source at https://science.nasa.gov/mission/roman-space-telescope/adopt-a-pixel/.
